clue.text: Punctuation mark perhaps too irregular

indicators.note: irregular means not in proper order, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grammarian wonders whether a punctuation mark has been used too erratically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' looks like a qualifier on the surface but is part of the anagram fodder with 'too'; 'irregular' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: This mark shows possession or omitted letters, so it is one of the standard punctuation symbols.

clue.text: Powerful fellow supports joke

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits below it, so the fellow comes after the joke

parts.note: a pun is a joke playing on words
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A strong man props up a gag, like a comic's straight man.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or remark is strong and sharp, so powerful in effect.

clue.text: Energetic secret agent captures traitor, finally

indicators.note: captures means the agent's letters close around and hold the other piece

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word traitor

explanation.surface: A lively spy seizes a turncoat at the end of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone, often older, who is nimble and full of energy.

clue.text: Give in regarding period for abstinence

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
Lent is the forty days before Easter when Christians give things up

explanation.surface: Someone yields on the matter of a time of fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and yield, giving way after resisting.

clue.text: Hand over booze — It'll get you over the border!

definitions.text: It'll get you over the border!

parts.note: to pass something is to hand it over
port is a fortified wine, a kind of booze

explanation.surface: Smuggling drink across the frontier by handing it over.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: the travel document lets you cross national frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel document is shown at frontier controls to be allowed to cross into another country.

clue.text: Fix me up with piece of furniture

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a bed is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: An instruction to set someone up with a bed, like a hotel request.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to fix it firmly in a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Thwarted clumsy fraudster pocketing wallet, ultimately

indicators.note: pocketing means the jumbled letters take the other piece inside them
clumsy suggests something handled badly and jumbled, so the letters of fraudster are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word wallet

explanation.surface: An inept con man is foiled while lifting a wallet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clumsy' rearranges FRAUDSTER, and 'pocketing' puts the T from 'wallet, ultimately' inside that anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thwarted means having your aims blocked, which is what frustrated describes.

clue.text: Young lady hugs retreating Frenchman — typical!

indicators.note: hugs means the young lady's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl or young woman

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the Frenchman's name is reversed

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A girl embraces a Frenchman who is backing away; how predictable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'typical' is an adjective, so the answer is general in its everyday sense, not the army officer the surface suggests; 'retreating' and 'hugs' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: General as an adjective means common or usual, as in the general case, hence typical.

clue.text: Dazzling girl initially making a mess

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word girl

parts.note: littering is making a mess by dropping rubbish

explanation.surface: A girl starts out by leaving her things everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Glittering means sparkling brilliantly, so dazzling to the eye.

clue.text: Solemn robes altered

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of robes are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Ceremonial robes have been tailored for a grave occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sober can mean serious and earnest in manner, a synonym of solemn.

clue.text: Chilled and cut up, with head removed

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken away here

parts.note: diced means cut up into small cubes

explanation.surface: A recipe step: chill the meat and cut it up after removing the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something iced has been cooled with ice, so it is chilled.

clue.text: Trendy suit, to a large degree

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy
spades is one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A fashionable suit worn to great effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in great abundance or very much, so to a large degree.

clue.text: Criminal or genial local

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or corrupted, so the letters of or genial are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the man in the local pub a crook or a friendly sort?
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' looks like a noun for a pub or resident, but it is the adjective defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional means belonging to a particular area rather than the whole country, as local does.

clue.text: Theist arranged donations to the church

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so the letters of theist are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A believer organised gifts for the parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tithes were tenths of produce or income given to support the clergy and church.

clue.text: A republican badly hurt legendary king

indicators.note: badly suggests something done wrong, so the letters of hurt are jumbled

explanation.surface: A republican has wounded a mythical monarch, a fitting enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: The king of Camelot in British legend, leader of the Knights of the Round Table.

clue.text: Talk tediously about old hunting weapon

indicators.note: about means the phrase for talking tediously goes around the other piece

parts.note: to harp on is to keep talking tediously about one subject

explanation.surface: Someone drones on about an antique whaling weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbed spear thrown or fired at whales and large fish is used in hunting them.

clue.text: Recline under mountain pass for sheepdog

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the reclining word below the pass, so after it

parts.note: a col is a low pass between mountain peaks
to lie is to recline

explanation.surface: A sheepdog lies down beneath a high pass in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: This Scottish breed is the classic herding dog used to work sheep.

clue.text: Before end of sermon, religious leader to speak for ages

indicators.note: before means the preceding pieces come ahead of the sermon's final letter

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious leader

indicators.note: end of points to the last letter of the word sermon

explanation.surface: A rabbi drones on as his sermon nears its close.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is British informal speech for chattering at length; it comes from rhyming slang, rabbit and pork for talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to chatter on at tedious length, so to talk for a long time.

clue.text: Not finishing, freezing cold curry

indicators.note: not finishing means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: baltic is British slang for freezing cold

explanation.surface: A curry left unfinished has gone stone cold.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTIC is British (especially Scottish) slang for extremely cold, after the chilly Baltic Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy dish cooked and served in a wok-like metal bowl, a type of curry.

clue.text: Worry forfeit is regularly ignored

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter of forfeit is dropped, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: Worrying about a penalty that is routinely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and troubled, a synonym of to worry.

clue.text: Loos redesigned for European capital

indicators.note: redesigned means remade in a new form, so the letters of loos are reordered

explanation.surface: The public toilets of a European capital have been remodelled.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the capital of Norway, in northern Europe.

clue.text: Material found in ebony longbow

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit within the run of the words ebony longbow

explanation.surface: A fabric discovered in a dark wooden archery bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A synthetic polymer fibre woven into fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Caught young woman with dictionary

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl or young woman
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A girl was caught with a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Being roped with a noose, as a cowboy does with cattle, means being caught.

clue.text: What an escapologist might say — I'm sure of it!

definitions.meaning: read literally, a performer announcing they will be tied up with ropes and chains
an exclamation of certainty, meaning I'm confident it is so

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned assertion of certainty, while literally it predicts being tied up.
